## Demo 1: Ask a Bare LLM

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(player_bare(height=340))
```

[The Claude and ChatGPT apps *can* answer this for real stocks, because
the apps are agents: they wrap the model in a loop with web search and
code tools. HSKY and JNTH stand in for **your own data**, which no model
has seen.]{.muted .fragment style="font-size:0.75em"}

## What Is an LLM Agent?

::: {.bigidea}
An LLM in a **loop** that picks a **tool**, reads the **result**, and
repeats until it can answer [@yao2023react].
:::

The model **never runs code**. It writes a JSON request, and our code
runs it [@schick2023toolformer].

## The Whole Agent Loop {.loopcode}

```{python}
#| output: asis
src = inspect.getsource(run_agent)
print('```{.python code-line-numbers="|5|6-8|9-12|14-15|16"}')
print(src + "```")
```

[**5** model picks a move]{.pill .good} [**6-8** done? stop]{.pill .ok}
[**9-12** run the tool, catch errors]{.pill .good}
[**14-15** feed the result back]{.pill .ok}
[**16** step cap]{.pill .good}

## Did It Get the Right Answer?

Check the agent against pandas, computed directly from the CSV:

```{python}
#| echo: true
wide = PRICES.pivot(index="date", columns="ticker", values="close")
ret = (wide.iloc[-1] / wide.iloc[0] - 1) * 100
ret.round(2)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"::: {{.bigidea}}\n**Agent:** {FINAL}\n:::")
```

Same numbers. Every price came from `get_prices` and every percent from
`calculator`: the **model plans, the tools compute**, and the trace is an
audit log.

## When Agents Break: Endless Loops

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(player("loop", height=500))
```

Fix: always cap steps (and cost), and let tools say a task is impossible.

## Other Ways Agents Fail

::: {.incremental}
- **Bad tool arguments:** a typo like `HUSKY` breaks the call, so return
  errors that say how to recover
- **Untrusted tool output:** text in a web page or file can hijack the
  agent, called prompt injection [@greshake2023injection]
- **Nondeterminism:** the same question can produce a different trace
  every run
- **Overkill:** if a fixed pipeline works, you may not need an agent
  [@anthropic2024agents]
:::

## How Good Is Your Agent? A Stats Question

Each test task is a Bernoulli trial, so report a Wilson confidence
interval [@wilson1927], not one good demo.

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(ci_widget())
```

[17 of 20 looks like 85%, but it could be 64% to 95%. At 85% per run,
5 straight passes happen only `{python} round(100 * 0.85 ** 5)`% of
the time.]{.muted}

## Takeaways

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="32%"}
::: {.card .take}
[01]{.grad style="font-size:2.2em;font-weight:800"}

An agent is an **LLM in a loop with tools**: the model plans, your code
does the work.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
::: {.card .take}
[02]{.grad style="font-size:2.2em;font-weight:800"}

Put facts and math in **tools**, and keep the **trace** so every number
is auditable.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
::: {.card .take}
[03]{.grad style="font-size:2.2em;font-weight:800"}

Guard the loop with **step caps and clear errors**, and measure success
with **intervals, not one demo**.
:::
:::
::::

## Further Readings

- [Building effective AI agents][bea], when to use agents vs. simple
  workflows
- [Claude tool use docs][tu], the real request and response format behind
  `record.py`
- [ReAct paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629), the reason
  then act pattern used in this deck
- [Toolformer paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761), how models learn
  to call tools
- [SWE-bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770), a benchmark that grades
  agents on real GitHub issues

[bea]: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
[tu]: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview

## Resources {.smaller}

- **Code in this folder**
  - `agent.py`: tools, the agent loop, replay model, and widget helpers
  - `player.tpl`, `ci.tpl`: HTML for the in-slide demos (no external
    libraries)
  - `make_data.py`: simulated prices and seed traces (fixed seed)
  - `record.py`: optional, re-records traces from a real model

  - `data/prices.csv`, `data/traces.json`, `figures/hero.svg`,
